name: resource-relationship
title: Resource Relationship
description: A relationship of one rdfs:Resource (http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#Resource) to another, or to a simple named concept.
comments: Resources can be thought of as identifiable records or instances of classes and may include, but need not be limited to instances of ltc:ObjectGroup, ltc:OrganisationalUnit, ltc:Taxon, ltc:Event, ltc:GeographicContext, ltc:GeologicalContext, ltc:EcologicalContext, or ltc:ObjectClassification. In the context of Latimer Core, the main purposes of this class are 1. to define different semantic and hierarchical relationships between ObjectGroups, and 2. to support quantified and annotated relationships between ObjectGroups and other LtC classes (such as ltc:Taxon and ltc:GeographicContext) and properties (such as ltc:discipline and ltc:objectType) that describe the contents of the ObjectGroup, using the hasMeasurementOrFact property.
rdfs:comment: A relationship of one rdfs:Resource (http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#Resource) to another, or to a simple named concept.

fields.name: resourceRelationship_pk
fields.title: Resource Relationship (Primary Key)
fields.description: A unique identifier for an ltc:ResourceRelationship.
fields.comments: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to guarantee uniqueness.
fields.rdfs:comment: A unique identifier for an ltc:ResourceRelationship.

fields.name: relatedResourceID
fields.title: Related Resource ID
fields.description: An identifier for a related resource (the object, rather than the subject of the relationship).
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for the related resource (the object) of a dwc:ResourceRelationship.

fields.name: relatedResourceName
fields.title: Related Resource Name
fields.description: A short textual name for the related resource.
fields.comments: This property can be used to list resources related to the source entity which lack an identifier, for example if a separate record for that resource doesn't yet exist. In the Collection Description standard, a use of this is to list named subcollections of a larger collections at a time when the resources might not be available to create a full Collection Description for each of them. If at a later point a Collection Description record is created for the subcollection, an identifier can be added to the relatedResourceID property to maintain the same relationship.
fields.examples: `FMNH Mammals`, `TNHC Vertebrates`, `Sloane Herbarium`, `Grant Southwest Ceramics Collection`
fields.rdfs:comment: A short textual name for the related resource.

fields.name: relatedResourceType
fields.title: Related Resource Type
fields.description: The class or property within Latimer Core, or class, property or less formal concept outside of the Latimer Core standard, that is represented by the related resource.
fields.comments: This property can be used to explicitly define the type of resource that the ID stored in the relatedResourceID property references, either to support IDs that don’t fully resolve and provide contextual metadata, or just for information purposes. It can also provide context for use cases where the relatedResourceName is used rather than the relatedResourceID to define the target, for example to attach a simple list of the names of related collections to an ObjectGroup.
fields.rdfs:comment: The class or property within Latimer Core, or class, property or less formal concept outside of the Latimer Core standard, that is represented by the related resource.

fields.name: relationshipAccordingTo
fields.title: Relationship According To
fields.description: The source (person, organization, publication, reference) establishing the relationship between the two resources.
fields.rdfs:comment: The source (person, organization, publication, reference) establishing the relationship between the two resources.

fields.name: relationshipEstablishedDate
fields.title: Relationship Established Date
fields.description: The date-time on which the relationship between the two resources was established.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a date that conforms to ISO 8601-1:2019.
fields.rdfs:comment: The date-time on which the relationship between the two resources was established.

fields.name: relationshipOfResource
fields.title: Relationship Of Resource
fields.description: The relationship of the resource identified by relatedResourceID to the subject (optionally identified by the resourceID).
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. https://schema.org/Property
fields.rdfs:comment: The relationship of the resource identified by relatedResourceID to the subject (optionally identified by the resourceID).

fields.name: relationshipRemarks
fields.title: Relationship Remarks
fields.description: Comments or notes about the relationship between the two resources.
fields.examples: `The Darwin fossil collection makes up part of the museum's palaeontology collection.`, `Some of the same Madagascan bryophytes are included in both of these collections.`
fields.rdfs:comment: Comments or notes about the relationship between the two resources.

fields.name: resourceID
fields.title: Resource ID
fields.description: An identifier for the resource that is the subject of the relationship.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for the resource that is the subject of the relationship.
